sources.title: ReHLDS engine sv_main.cpp - SV_BanId_f, SV_RemoveId_f, SV_WriteId_f, SV_GetIDString, rcon_password cvar
ReHLDS engine host_cmd.cpp - Host_Status_f output format, Host_Kick_f, say command registration
Console Command List - Valve Developer Community (banid, removeid, kick, say)
ENSL/NS - Natural Selection mod for Half-Life source (mod folder ns)
Natural Selection HLDS Setup Guide - Unknown Worlds Forums (hlds.exe -console -game nsp +port ... +map ...)

notes: Natural Selection is a Half-Life 1 (GoldSrc) mod with no dedicated-server app of its own: it is run by HLDS as 'hlds -console -game ns +port 27015 +map ns_eclipse' (the ENSL/NS repository is the mod folder 'ns'; the Unknown Worlds setup thread shows the same shape of invocation against the older 'nsp' folder, e.g. 'hlds.exe -console -game nsp +port 27014 +maxplayers 10 +map co_angst'). Moderation is therefore pure GoldSrc engine, not mod-specific, and every command string here was read out of the ReHLDS engine source (a reverse-engineering of HLDS build 6152/6153) and re-verified against it line by line: SV_BanId_f prints 'Usage:  banid <minutes> <uniqueid or #userid> { kick }' plus 'Use 0 minutes for permanent'; SV_RemoveId_f prints 'Usage:  removeid <uniqueid | #slotnumber>'; Host_Kick_f prints 'usage:  kick < name > | < # userid >' in stock builds and gains '[reason]' only when compiled with REHLDS_FIXES, so {reason} is deliberately absent from the kick template. Host_Kick_f matches a bare first argument against the player NAME only; it does additionally have a '#'-prefixed branch that will accept a Steam ID, but that path re-assembles the id out of several Cmd_Argv slots and is fragile, so the template uses {playerName} while ban/unban use the uniqueid. banid alone is in-memory only; bans survive a restart only after 'writeid', which rewrites the file named by the 'bannedcfgfile' cvar (registered default 'banned.cfg', in the mod directory) as lines of the form 'banid 0.0 STEAM_0:1:12345678' (SV_WriteId_f: FS_FPrintf(f, "banid 0.0 %s\n", SV_GetIDString(...))). IP bans are a separate system (addip/removeip/writeip -> listip.cfg) and are not modelled here. RCON is GoldSrc RCON - a challenge/response UDP protocol on the same port as the game - and is NOT the Source RCON TCP wire protocol, hence flavour 'custom'; rcon_password is the only enable-like cvar registered (the sv_rcon_* cvars are failure-threshold and ban-penalty tuning, not an on/off switch) and RCON cannot be moved off the game port. The status output is taken verbatim from Host_Status_f: the header '#      name userid uniqueid frag time ping loss adr', then per client '#%2i %8s %i %s' where the %8s argument is va("\"%s\"", client->name) - so the name is always quoted and the column order really is name, userid, uniqueid - followed by frags, time, ping, loss and, only when printing to the local console (conprint) rather than over RCON, the address; the block ends with a '%i users' line. Fake clients print 'BOT' in the uniqueid column. SV_GetIDString also emits non-numeric ids that are NOT Steam IDs: 'STEAM_ID_PENDING' while a client is still authenticating, 'STEAM_ID_LAN' / 'VALVE_ID_LAN' when sv_lan is 1, 'VALVE_ID_PENDING', 'VALVE_ID_LOOPBACK' for a loopback client and 'HLTV' for the proxy; linePattern now accepts these so the roster is not silently empty on a LAN or unauthenticated server, but they are placeholders and must never be passed to banid. Many NS servers additionally run Metamod/AMX Mod X, which layers its own amx_kick/amx_ban commands on top; the engine commands above work regardless.
